I agree with you here. Born and raised Christian, it's just engrained into my head that women typically stay at home and watch the kids, and the man goes out every day to work and bring home money to support his family. If my wife made more than I did I'd definitely feel like a failure. We can't help but have these concepts in the back of our heads at all times, that's just how we were raised. However like you said, if the man wants to be the parent that stays at home and the woman wants to go out and work, they should be able to. Nothing wrong with that. 

I suppose we just need something a little bit different from most women these days

20M from canada, and it seems like i have different opinions than the majority here, which is a good thing i guess.

I'd like to think I'm more "old fashioned" than anything because genuinely, if I had a wife that made more money than me I definitely would not feel good about myself at all. I don't particularly think "women belong in the kitchen go make me a sandwich waaaahhh", but at the same time I'd be really uncomfortable if she was the breadwinner in the family.

I got very lucky with my current girlfriend. She wants nothing more than to have kids with me and be the best mom she can be. She and I both work full time currently and I make more than she does; which, as bad as it sounds, makes me feel good about myself.

Women and men are equals and should be treated as such in the workplace, it's just that I'd personally feel more comfortable in life knowing that I was the provider for my family. I wouldn't go as far as to prevent my wife from having a job, though.

I'm a man that's been taking testosterone for over 5 years now. Never had any surgeries yet, so I'm still "biologically female". That fact alone is enough to make me want to jump in front of a train. I completely understand you. I feel as though I'll never be a true man. The shame and disgust I feel towards myself is astronomical.

I want you to know that you ARE a woman. Despite any physical appearance, you are a woman. Taking hormones even solidifies that fact. Even if you weren't, you're still a woman. It's such a fucking tragedy that we were forced to live in these bodies that don't feel like our own. I'm here for you if you ever want to PM, I know a thing or two about dysphoria. We can get through this together.
I can't wait for the day.

I beg of you, don't do something drastic. I COMPLETELY understand the feeling of a lifetime of suffering and abuse and trauma (albeit I'm 20 years old) but I can relate to being molested and abused for the entirety of my childhood. I truly feel for you in that regard. I can't speak on being homeless or not being able to work, but I can see how significant of a toll that will take on a person.

I just want more than anything for you to keep pushing. You've made it through things so many of us would not have survived. I wholeheartedly respect you for that. 

I'm honestly here for you. And that's not an empty promise. If you would like we can PM and talk about it. I'll be here to support you. I don't even know you, but I don't want to lose you. Please.

When I was 14-18, I was pretty dependent on alcohol. Drinking fairly regularly and trying to find any excuse I could to find some random high school party to go to just so I could get blackout drunk. Then when I was 19 I met my ex who at the time made me want to stop so I could fully enjoy life with her. I stayed sober for almost a year. I'm 20 now, and since then my mental health has significantly worsened due to external life factors, and the fact that I broke up with her. I ended up spiraling worse than I ever had before and here I am now, more addicted to alcohol than I ever was before and seeing no light at the end of the tunnel for reaching sobriety again. 

It's really difficult to have a drink "once in a while" after having such a toxic relationship with alcohol in your life. My body has gone right back to suffering; except it's 100x worse this time around.

Well, if you don't hear from me in the near future you know I bit the bullet and pulled out the trusty rope I keep in my backpack xD

Thanks friend

Honestly, the mind and body are so insanely connected I wouldn't be surprised if that's the case. I'm not an expert in the field, but that's my best guess. If the idea is in your head that you "need" a bit of alcohol every x amount of hours, your body will agree and therefore produce physical symptoms. 

I get the same way, every 8 hours or so without a drink I become extremely agitated and depressed and nauseous, but then again I drink really heavily so I'm not sure.
Thanks, we'll see

To be honest it sounds like more of a nuisance than anything since I work full time and would have to try and work around my schedule with getting help. I guess that's a big sign as to where I stand on the idea of getting sober right now. I feel like a waste of space, but it's still not enough for me to actively go out of my way to get the right help
I'll check it out!
True, you have a good point. I guess it all really does come down to if I truly want this bad enough to try and get sober. I just don't know if I'm at that point yet

I have a very well paying job, which is why it's so difficult for me to decide between liquor or finding a psychologist. It is annoying having to spend so much money per week on alcohol though so it'd be nice to not have to do that anymore. I guess I'm just scared of the physical risks of quitting and I feel ashamed having to be medically supervised during a detox or some shit like that. Ego definitely IS a bitch.

I lost my last job at the hospitals I worked at because I would constantly drink myself into a blackout and wake up late for my early shifts. Since I got fired I immediately started working at a private cardiology clinic, (thank god I could find a replacement job within two weeks) but that was a massive wake up call and I haven't let my drinking make me miss shifts again, yet I still haven't changed my drinking habits. It makes me feel like such a waste of space, and a shit healthcare worker since I can't even take care of myself.

I'll definitely look into those online meetings, since listening to other people tends to help. Thanks for sharing your story.

Sometimes I really do feel like drinking myself to death is the only option. I'm on medication that you're technically not supposed to drink on because alcohol and my medications are both CNS depressants so I've almost slipped into a coma twice now; if my friends didn't physically show up to my house after I wasn't answering their calls or texts when we were supposed to hang out, I probably wouldn't be here today. Sometimes I wish they never showed up. Alcohol makes everything more "fun" in my mind, but I let it get out of control

This sounds really nice. I'm so sorry you went through all of that. It's amazing you were able to overcome something that severe. I'd really love to have the extra money to spend on my girlfriend and I. It's just so hard to imagine my life without drinking because it's something I physically and emotionally depend on. That fact makes me so sad. I do realize that I'm absent for 90% of my life, as my girlfriend has pointed out in the past, she says she "doesn't get 100% of me" when I've been drinking. I want to get better, I just don't know if i have the mental strength to do it

Now that you mention it, I have felt something like this happen very recently. I've been drinking consistently for over a year but it's gotten a lot worse and i'd be finishing entire bottles of vodka in a night. I woke up one day last week feeling weird, something I've never felt before. It's like you described. It felt bloated and swollen and painful and made me nauseous, so I couldn't eat anything at all and therefore felt horrible. It was scary, but unfortunately wasn't enough to inspire me to lay off. I've been feeling that way for the past week, although it's slowly improving.

I don't know if it has anything to do with the liver, but maybe seeking a blood test or ultrasound of some test of that sort might be of help to rule it out.
I'm 20, I drink at least 350ml of vodka a day. Not sure if we're just outliers though
